en.title: Evaluate Nested Add/Subtract Expressions
en.description:
An expression is an integer, or add(x,y) or sub(x,y), where the arguments can themselves be expressions. add means addition, and sub means the first argument minus the second. The input is valid; spaces may appear between tokens, and integers may be negative. Find the result.

The input format, examples, and test data are compiled and written by CSWork.
en.input: A single line containing the expression, of length 1..200000. Integers and the final result are within the 32-bit signed integer range; use sufficiently wide integers for intermediate values. Integers contain no internal spaces.
en.output: Output the answer as described; multiple results are separated by spaces, in order.
en.explanation: The example inputs and outputs follow the rules above directly; see the solution for the full algorithm.
hints: Lexically scan for add, sub, signed integers, and right parentheses. Use an operator stack and a value stack; whenever a right parenthesis appears, pop two values and perform one operation, which avoids deep recursion.
